findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/generation-metadata.tex, the author-study \AIModelContribution declaration, its iteration-5 clause: "together with two standing advisories --- the second reading's closing remark about what that reading claims of the Postcommunion removed, ... and the third reading's use of Aquinas on Dan 9:18 recorded in the interpretation audit, whose witnesses, element table and moral sense now agree with the manifest and the section"
findings.problem: The record claims a repair that was not made. research/interpretations.md, whose sealed bytes I read in full, names Thomas Aquinas nowhere in section 3: not among the just-judge-merciful-hearer reading's witnesses in 3.2, not in the 3.3 Offertory row (which still reads 'Jerome on 9:5-23; Augustine De pecc. mer. II sect. 13; Rupert, Durandus (chant)'), not in the 3.4 moral sense, and not in the summary table's row for that lane, which still lists 'Augustine; Jerome; Cassiodorus; Hilary; Robert Bellarmine; with Rupert and Durandus for the chants'. The file's own header note records revisions through the fourth reentry only and none at this iteration, and the file is unmodified since the last commit. So the three things the clause asserts -- that the audit records Aquinas, and that its witnesses, element table and moral sense now agree with proper-components.toml (which does declare him for that lane) and with sections/40-just-judge-merciful-hearer.tex (which does develop him at length, on Super Philippenses c. 4, on 4:6) -- are each false, and only one of the two advisories the clause reports cleared was in fact cleared: STU-012 was, STU-006 was not. The leaf's own production audit states the opposite of the generation record, in terms and with its reason: research/production-review.md carries a heading '`STU-006`, advisory, not cleared, and why', and explains that research/interpretations.md belongs to the research stage and that repairing it from author-study 'would be a silent revision of a reviewed upstream document, which the workflow contract forbids'. That entry is right; the generation record contradicts it. Nothing of this reaches a reader of the PDF, because the contribution declarations render only the revision timestamp. What is damaged is the tracked record itself: guidance/editorial.md, 'Audit records and generation metadata', makes these declarations 'the complete tracked audit record' of what produced the document, and this one now reports as done a repair the leaf does not contain and cannot contain until its research owner makes it. The leaf therefore carries two permanent, contradictory statements about what this iteration did, and the one a later production or maintainer meets first is the false one. The defect is new this round, since the clause was written this round, and repairing it moves no reader-facing text and no pagination.
findings.required_result: The author-study contribution declaration states what iteration 5 actually did: the STU-011 repair, the one advisory it cleared (STU-012, the second reading's closing remark on the Postcommunion), and STU-006 left uncleared and reported to its owner, in agreement with the 'STU-006, advisory, not cleared, and why' entry of research/production-review.md. It claims no clearance of STU-006 and no agreement of research/interpretations.md section 3 with the manifest and the section. The study stage corrects the record rather than making the claim true: research/interpretations.md is the research stage's file, as the audit entry itself establishes, so recording Aquinas there is not this owner's to do.

findings.location: research/interpretations.md section 3 (3.2 'Principal witnesses and their reasoning', the 3.3 element table's Offertory row, the 3.4 moral sense, and the lane's row in 'The three readings in brief'), against sections/40-just-judge-merciful-hearer.tex, 'Daniel's prayer and Daniel's people' (PDF p. 27) and that reading's moral sense (PDF p. 30)
findings.problem: Standing advisory from study-review iterations 0, 2, 3 and 4, still uncleared at iteration 5 and restated because this stage's entries replace its previous ones in evaluations/blocking-findings-v1.toml. proper-components.toml declares Thomas Aquinas among the just-judge-merciful-hearer lane's authors, and the study develops him there -- 'prayer must be made with confidence of obtaining, and that confidence comes from God's mercy', Super Philippenses c. 4, on 4:6, on Dan 9:18 -- and credits him by name in that reading's moral sense. research/interpretations.md section 3 still does not, at any of its four loci. The evidence is sound and independently checked: research/scope.md 3.7 records the locus, the Dessain 1857 vol. 2 p. 398 page image read, and exactly the source role the study uses ('Aquinas uses Dan 9:18 as doctrine on prayer; he does not expound Daniel'). No reader of the PDF meets a false claim; what is broken is the correspondence between the manifest, the interpretation audit and the section, which those records exist to make inspectable. It stays advisory: the severity was decided when the defect was first seen and does not change because the round has come round again.
findings.required_result: research/interpretations.md section 3 records Thomas Aquinas among the just-judge-merciful-hearer reading's witnesses, with his locus (Super Philippenses c. 4, on 4:6) and the source role research/scope.md 3.7 gives him, and his name in the 3.3 Offertory row, the 3.4 moral sense and the lane's row in the summary table, so that the audit record, the manifest and the section agree. Until its research owner does that, no record of the leaf may state that it has been done.

findings.location: sections/05-appointed-texts.tex, the note after the Gospel ('Ps 109:1 in verse 44', PDF p. 6), and the later uses at sections/10-each-element.tex ('Ps~109:1'), sections/30-son-and-lord-of-david.tex (four uses, including the anagogical sense) and sections/50-comparison.tex
findings.problem: Ps 109 is the one psalm the study cites that never carries its modern number. The head of sections/05 states the study's convention -- 'Psalms are cited in the Missal's numbering, with the Hebrew numbering in parentheses' -- and the 1962 profile requires the same ('Psalm citations use the missal's Vulgate/Septuagint numbering first, with the common modern number in parentheses where it differs'). Every other psalm obeys it at first use: Ps 118 (Heb. 119), Ps 32 (Heb. 33), Ps 101 (Heb. 102:2; 102:1 where the title is not numbered), Ps 75 (Heb. 76:12-13; 76:11-12 ...), and the apparatus even gives Ps 13:1 (Heb. 14:1) and Ps 52:2 (Heb. 53:2). Ps 109 is Hebrew Ps 110, and it is the hinge of the whole second reading: it is the verse Christ quotes in the appointed Gospel, the text of Augustine's Enarratio that opens that reading, and the citation printed in its anagogical sense. Because the preamble promises the parenthesis wherever the numbering differs, its absence reads as an assurance that it does not differ here, and a reader who turns to Ps 109 in a modern psalter finds 'O God, be not thou silent in my praise', not 'The Lord said to my Lord'. The number given is correct in the study's declared system and the words of the verse are printed wherever it is cited, so no reader of this study alone is misled about the text -- which is why this does not block.
findings.required_result: Ps 109 carries its modern number in parentheses at its first use in the body, as the study's other psalms do -- Ps 109:1 (Heb. 110:1) in the note after the Gospel in sections/05-appointed-texts.tex -- so that the convention the same page states holds for every psalm the study cites. Later bare uses may stand as the other psalms' later bare uses do.

findings.location: sections/30-son-and-lord-of-david.tex, 'The other texts as confession', the Postcommunion paragraph, final clause: 'which the typical edition prints here merely as Per Dominum nostrum and which RG 115~a completes' (PDF p. 24)
findings.problem: 'RG' is never expanded where a reader of the body meets it. This is its only occurrence in the study's reader-facing argument, and the study cites the same rubric twice elsewhere in longhand: sections/05-appointed-texts.tex, at the Secret, writes 'the conclusion said is the full form of the general rubrics (no. 115 a)', and sections/00-opening.tex writes out 'Rubricae generales 111 b; Rubricae generales Missalis 434 b'. The abbreviation is used again in the terminal appendix ('RG 91, 111 b, 127 b; RGMR 427, 434 b, 494 b'), where the References on the following page do expand it, so a determined reader can decode it; a reader of the interpretation ten pages earlier cannot, and meets one citation form for a rubric the study has already given him in another. The defect is in clarity and internal consistency, not in the fact cited, which propers/verified.md section 8 supports.
findings.required_result: The clause cites the rubric in the form the body already uses -- the general rubrics, no. 115 a -- or the abbreviation is introduced once before it is used, so that no reader-facing sentence of the argument carries an unexplained abbreviation and the same rubric is cited one way throughout the body.

observations.location: sections/90-apparatus.tex, References: the entries for Rupert of Deutz (De divinis officiis XII.17-18) and St Robert Bellarmine (on Pss 32:6, 12; 75:9-13; 101:2; 118:1, 124, 137) (PDF pp. 37-38)
observations.note: Two reference loci reach slightly past what the study cites: the body uses Rupert at XII.17 only (XII.18, his Eighteenth Sunday, is discussed in research/scope.md 2.4 but reaches no claim in the study), and it uses Bellarmine on Ps 32:6 and 12, Ps 75, Ps 101:2 and Ps 118:124 and 137, but nowhere on Ps 118:1, which research/scope.md 3.1 records as read. The 1962 profile asks that References contain only sources actually used, with exact loci sufficient to verify their claims; each of these is one item wider than the claims it supports, which is ordinary scholarly latitude rather than an unused source, so it does not reach my criteria as a finding. I record it because a reader checking the apparatus against the body will find the mismatch. The Gregory entry, which an earlier round's observation grouped with these, is correct as printed: Homiliae in Evangelia 38.9-10 is right, because the paragraph's opening claim that the wedding garment is charity comes from 38.9 and only the rest from 38.10; if anything it is the body's own parenthesis, which cites 38.10 alone, that is the narrow one.

summary: Cold review of the expansive study liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost (main.tex; 38 physical pages, within the 20-50 contract; all 19 sealed files re-hashed and matched before reading). Checked independently: the three readings are distinguishable, internally coherent, each carries its own four senses and lets every one of the ten appointed elements contribute; all ten Latin blocks in sections/05 match propers/verified.md word for word; every Douay English block and every textual note (illumina/ostende at Dan 9:17, perveniat/veniat at Ps 101:2, Dominus Deus eorum at Ps 32:12, omnes before reges at Ps 75:13, Obsecro itaque vos at Eph 4:1, Ps 118:135 beside the Offertory) matches the tracked Clementine and Challoner verse texts; Chrysostom In Mt. hom. 71 and In Eph. hom. 9-11 were re-read whole in the tracked NPNF1 10 and 13 and every quotation, including the four alternating proof texts and the vainglory close, is exact; so are Augustine De doctrina I.22.20-21, I.27.28 and I.30.31-33, the Latin Enarrationes on Pss 32, 101 and 109, Jerome on Dan 9 at every quoted locus, Gregory Hom. in Ev. 38.9-10, Irenaeus Adv. haer. I.22.1 at ANF 1 p. 347, Bellarmine on Pss 32, 75, 101 and 118, and Schuster on the Ps 118 procession and the Gradual. STU-011 is fully repaired: the proof text now reads Ps 13:1 (Heb. 14:1), which is the psalm whose words the quotation prints, and the References disclose the NPNF1 10 note's 'Ps. liii. 1' against it. The terminal Scriptural Date and Location sheet, the reviewed home of the chronology the concise opening reprints, carries the generated projection unedited and keeps composition, narrated event, audience and geography apart. Limits of this review: sources the repository does not hold locally (Theodoret PG 82, Chrysostom's Greek in PG 62, Hilary in CSEL 22, Aquinas in Dessain and the Corpus Thomisticum, Rupert, Durandus, Gueranger, Trent, the Wilson sacramentaries) were checked against the leaf's own records and their recorded digests, not at their own page images. One blocking defect remains, and it is not in the reader-facing prose: the leaf's generation record states that an advisory was cleared at this iteration when it was not, and the leaf's own production audit says so in terms.
